sentence: Take v2 when size and speed matter: it gives up 2.7 points of accuracy against Smart Turn for a file of 0.63 MB instead of 8.7 MB and about 2.4 ms per decision in WASM instead of about 32 ms natively; take Smart Turn's file when those points matter more.

calibration.rules: temperature by validation NLL; tau50 = 0.5 on the calibrated probability; tau85 = the highest threshold whose validation END recall is >= 0.85 (§7); neither ever from test

rules.choice: validation accuracy at tau 0.5 on f32 weights (§6.4)
rules.distil: distil unless the hard-label arm is higher by more than 0.005
rules.stop: the best arm below 0.82 stops v2 (§6.5)

probe.rule: the first rung of R1-R4 whose WASM median is <= 4.0 ms (§4.4)

leakage.rule: docs/s6-ear2-prereg.md §3.2: dropped if the id is a test id, or if the sha256 of the 16-bit PCM of the last 128 x 80 ms frames (v1's test WAV tails) equals a test clip's
leakage.sentence_overlap: not checkable: spoken_text is empty in both sets

disclosure: **Disclosure (§11).** v2 was designed after v1's test results. Its design study read measurements made on 3,000 clips of the same test set: v1's two models per source, Smart Turn per source, Smart Turn with 8, 4, 3, 2 and 1 s of context, and the trailing silence of 1,500 clips. The 4 s window was chosen from Smart Turn's accuracy on those test clips, and the data change was motivated by per-source test results. The official test set is therefore partly in-sample for v2's design choices, though never for its weights: no test clip is trained on, and no threshold is chosen on test. eot-bench, which the design never read, is the cleaner check, and it is reported (§8.4).
